inventory: One perspective U-shaped magnet: both long arms, the complete curved joining end at upper right, both exposed end faces at lower left, outline strokes and dark/light shading survive.
The pale/rear arm carries the visible S and the dark/front arm carries the visible N. Both source pole labels remain inside the crop.

Five small pointed needle silhouettes with vertical stems survive: far left, lower left beside the S end, upper middle over the rear arm, middle/front between the arms, and below the N arm. The visible stem portions, including portions interrupted or hidden by the magnet, match the page.
The individual pointed ends and dark/light needle regions retain their differing drawn orientations. They are not replaced with one common direction.
No separate labeled normal, coordinate axis, numerical annotation or standalone vector arrow is visible in this source graphic.
findings: Compared directly with the complete fig-246 graphic on physical page 286. The curved magnet end, arm ends, all five needle shapes, stem extremities and S/N labels remain uncut.
No adjacent prose, figure-number caption, fig-247 artwork or page furniture is present in the crop.
No missing subpart, added graphic or changed stroke/shading arrangement was observed in the original-PNG visual comparison.
figures.laterAuthorBoundary: Retain the observed magnet, five needles, source pole labels and stroke relationships as source inventory. This crop PASS does not establish unseen needle-pole assignments or approve a modern field/topology interpretation.

inventory: Two side-by-side graphic components belong to the same source figure: a complete person on the left and an enlarged inclining-needle apparatus on the right. Neither component is optional crop content.

The person retains the complete head, hair/face/ear strokes, striped shirt, collar, belt, both arms and hands, trousers, both legs and both shoes. The extended hand and its small round object, including rim/interior strokes, survive.
The apparatus retains the entire horizontal top hanger, short descending support, rounded arch, both side uprights and the visible lower oblique frame strokes.

The lower central crossing/pivot region and diagonally tilted pointed needle survive, including the broad dark lower-left portion, narrow upper-right tip and the other visible oblique strokes around the lower assembly.
The source graphic has no lettered poles, labeled normal, numerical labels or separate labeled vector arrows. Pointed needle ends are graphic features, not newly assigned arrow or pole labels.
findings: Compared directly with the entire two-component fig-247 graphic on physical page 286. Both the person and the inclining-needle apparatus are present; the crop is not an apparatus-only extraction.
No clipping was observed at the person's hair, round hand-held object or shoes, or at the apparatus hanger, lower-left needle tip, upper-right tip and lower-right frame extremity.
No adjacent prose, figure-number caption, fig-246 artwork or page furniture is present. All source graphic components and visible strokes survive.
figures.laterAuthorBoundary: Use the complete person-plus-apparatus inventory. Do not discard the person or invent connections, pivot-axis geometry, pole names or a modern apparatus interpretation from this crop approval.

inventory: The main graphic contains one thick upright central line and two nested perspective elliptical outlines around it. The drawn interruptions and crossings of those outlines with the central line and needles survive.
An upward-pointing arrow is present above the main central line. Its tip and the source's small white separation from the thicker line are retained.

Six small needle silhouettes with short upright stems remain: four on the outer outline at upper left, upper right, lower left and lower right; two on the inner outline at left and right. Their pointed ends and dark/light regions match the source positions.

A separate lower auxiliary screw/turning pictogram remains below the main graphic: the upright pointed element with short helical-looking strokes, curved turning arrow around its lower portion and broad dark base. The separating white gap from the main upright line remains.
No S/N pole letters, labeled normal, coordinate labels or numerical values are present. The main upward arrow and lower curved arrow are the observed explicit arrows; no extra arrows are introduced.
findings: Compared directly with the full fig-248 graphic on physical page 287. Both elliptical outlines, all six needles/stems, the central line and its upper arrow, and the entire lower pictogram are retained.
No clipping was observed at the upper arrow, left/right outline extents, needle points, lower curved arrow or base.
No fig-249 coil or needle, figure-number caption, adjacent prose or page furniture leaks into the crop.
figures.laterAuthorBoundary: Preserve both outlines, all six needles and the separate lower pictogram. Their source-pixel arrangement is recorded without inventing a connection across the white gap, assigning unlabeled poles or approving modern vector/normal semantics.

inventory: One cylindrical coil drawn in perspective survives in full, including its left rounded outer contour, long curved winding strokes, dense upper-right dark strokes, right elliptical opening and visible interior strokes.
Short diagonal strokes along the upper surface and lower opening are retained together with the longer winding strokes. No exact turn count is asserted from the densely overlapping source drawing.
Both short downward-projecting terminal/lead strokes at the bottom left and bottom right of the coil survive.

Four separate pointed needle silhouettes with upright stems surround the coil: one left of it, one above it, one upper right and one middle right. All four dark/light ends, stems and differing drawn orientations remain.
No pole letters, labeled normal, numerical label or separate vector arrow is visible. The needles' upright stems are not evidence of wires connecting them to the coil.
findings: Compared directly with the complete fig-249 graphic on physical page 287. The winding body, right opening, interior/shading strokes, both lower leads and all four surrounding needles are present.
No clipping was observed at the upper needle stem, left needle, rightmost needle tip, coil perimeter or either downward lead.
No fig-248 outline or pictogram, figure-number caption, adjacent prose or page furniture is present in the crop.
